title: The Ups and Downs of Working in Hong Kong

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Hey! How have you been doing recently, Derik?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: So far I...am the usual. Working on photography.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Whoa, you do photography?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes I do!

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Er...what do you photograph, usually?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I make magazine covers...that’s the main job anyway.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Ah, magazines? Which magazine? Do I know it?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: The magazine is called 100Most. It...is published on a weekly basis, and focuses on the hottest topics of the week. It’s mostly an entertainment magazine that isn’t particularly informative, which means it doesn’t report news.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I’ve read 100Most before – it’s really famous right now!

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Er yeah they’re pretty well-known. They’re doing a good job, they are.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: It’s them who are well-known, not you.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Not me, that’s why...I’m still pretty broke. Okay Okay Okay.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: It’s still a lot of fun, shooting for their covers.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Haven’t they recently been working less on their magazine and more on online media?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes indeed, they even started...uh making videos a while ago.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I see.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yeah, they’re working on...uh commercials, which are pretty funny. Like, the commercials they make have such interesting content that they’d...they might make you watch them a few times, even though you know they’re commercials. Because they feature artists that they (you) like, or topics that are currently very much discussed, which resonates with them (you/viewers) and entice them to watch more.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I see, are you involved in that part (of 100Most) then?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Not at all!

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Not at all. Which is...

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Because...they’ve invited me to help out, but uh their video team is so outstanding that I couldn’t possibly step in (find my niche), so I decided to focus on the magazine covers and photo shoots instead.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I have heard of their magazine before, but I’ve been so busy that I haven’t had the time to read it.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Oh, you...don’t really have to buy it, it’s fine. You get a lot of the information online anyway.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I do?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: You do *laughs* so uh...what about you? What are you working on at the moment?

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Me right now? Er...I recently resigned.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Ah...so you’re done with working.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Uh...I’m not quite done yet. Er...but I was working at a recruitment agency. But you know that already. Whereas now I’m working...eh I’m starting to learn programming.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Programming? What kind of programs...smartphone apps or computer programs or...

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: ...eh I might move on to smartphones later, but for the time being I’m working on web development, as in the websites you visit on your computer all the time.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Hmm...for watching videos?

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Watching videos? Not really. I’m planning to write an application that is...uh an online shopping platform. Isn’t it all the rage right now? Like taobao, and stuff like that.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Aha! So you’re planning to launch Hong Kong’s own Taobao, aren’t you?

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Uh...I wish I could make it that successful too.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: So...are you going to program a system so that someone will buy it, or do you already have certain goods that you plan to sell?

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: I don’t...have any goods yet...yeah but I hope that maybe...like...if a friend like you, say you want to sell a camera, you can have me make a site...so we can sell [stuff] together as well.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I see. No I’m not selling cameras; on the contrary, I’ve got to buy cameras. I want to buy some cameras on your site.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Ah, so you want to buy cameras. That works too. If I have them in stock, that is.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: As long as I get a discount!

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Yeah...but to be honest, developing a site is...well I’m just starting out to learn it, so it’s still quite difficult for me.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: How exactly is it difficult?

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: The difficult part is...I don’t know how to do it. Plus it’s actually pretty pricey to take those courses.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Isn’t YouTube already full of instructions (idiom: ‘with pictures and text’)? It should be easy enough.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Right! That’s true. So at the moment I’m depending totally on YouTube.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: I..also depend on YouTube anyway. I’m learning photography with YouTube as my teacher/mentor.

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Yeah...okay...so uh, yeah right now, frankly, I’m not able to make money through web development yet, so I can’t pay any tuition. Like say you’re trying to find a job, and you’ve got to...yeah, you...you’ve got to shell out to learn that (skill), but you don’t have the money yet, so it’s...there’s the difficulty.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Either way, to work freelance is to keep learning. So...keep it up, both of us!

lines.speaker: Li Chun Ho
lines.english: Yes, we should both keep it up! That’s about it.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yup. Okay。 Okay. Okay.
